Sovereign Canadian Digital Trade Infrastructure

Infrastructure canadienne souveraine de commerce numérique

TransPacific Trade Nexus (TPTN) is a sovereign digital trade operating environment for Canadian exporters and their international counterparties. Trade data and records align to international standards once — supporting readiness verification and coordinated cross-actor workflows across the corridor.

TransPacific Trade Nexus (TPTN) est un environnement opérationnel de commerce numérique souverain pour les exportateurs canadiens et leurs contreparties internationales. Les données et dossiers commerciaux s'alignent sur les normes internationales une seule fois — soutenant la vérification de la préparation et les flux de travail coordonnés entre les acteurs du corridor.

Platform Architecture & GovernanceArchitecture de l'infrastructure et gouvernance
Shared Infrastructure & Governance ViewVue Infrastructure Partagée & Gouvernance
The five operating workspaces above are connected through a shared sovereign infrastructure backbone. This dedicated architecture view documents the shared layers — Data Exchange Hub, standards alignment (WCO / UN/CEFACT / MLETR / CAN/DGSI-aligned governance), auditability, role-based access control, HITL governance, AI Trade Agent posture, multilingual readiness, ESG layer, and Canadian sovereign hosting — for policy, procurement, and government stakeholders.Les cinq espaces de travail ci-dessus sont reliés par un socle d'infrastructure souveraine partagée. Cette vue d'architecture dédiée documente les couches communes — Data Exchange Hub, alignement sur les normes (WCO / UN/CEFACT / MLETR / gouvernance alignée CAN/DGSI), auditabilité, contrôle d'accès basé sur les rôles, gouvernance HITL, posture de l'Agent IA Commerce, préparation multilingue, couche ESG et hébergement souverain canadien — à l'intention des parties prenantes en matière de politique, d'approvisionnement et de gouvernement.

AI Trade Agent — HS Code & Compliance AssistAgent IA Commerce — Assistance codes SH & conformité
When a new listing is created, the AI Trade Agent suggests an HS code based on your product description and flags known permit or certification requirements for your target markets. Example: "Product description matches Industrial Control Equipment — suggested HS 8537.10. Note: export to Vietnam and Republic of Korea may require an Export Permit under the Export Control List. Confirm classification before publishing."
AI classification suggestions require exporter confirmation before use. HS code determinations remain the legal responsibility of the exporter. The AI provides its reasoning with each suggestion.Les suggestions de classification de l'IA nécessitent la confirmation de l'exportateur avant utilisation. Les déterminations de code SH restent la responsabilité légale de l'exportateur. L'IA fournit son raisonnement avec chaque suggestion.

ESG & Sustainability — Listing LevelESG & Durabilité — Niveau de la fiche
The ESG layer is embedded across the product catalogue. Exporters can attach recognised third-party certifications (Organic, FSC, Fairtrade) at the listing level. These are recorded in the exporter's Sustainability Profile and available to buyers on request.

Products in categories with known environmental risk (e.g. deforestation-linked commodities) are flagged automatically. Human override is available with a documented justification, which is logged to the audit trail.

Integration with third-party carbon registries and certification bodies is planned for Phase 2. Current prototype shows illustrative metadata only.

AI
AI Trade Agent — Document Preparation
The AI Trade Agent auto-populates standard customs documentation using order and product data — Commercial Invoice fields, Customs Declaration entries, and Packing List details. Fields completed by AI are highlighted for exporter review. If the AI is uncertain about a field, it leaves it blank rather than guessing. All auto-populated content must be confirmed by the exporter before submission.
Advisory only — human confirmation required at each stage. The AI Trade Agent does not submit documents on behalf of the exporter. All AI actions are logged to the Activity Log.
AI Trade Agent — Inline Decision SupportAgent IA Commerce — Aide à la décision en lignePersistent desktop assistant · Advisory only · All actions loggedAssistant de bureau persistant · Consultatif · Toutes actions consignées
▲ Exporter asked: "Why was ORD-2026-PR-0221 flagged?"▲ L'exportateur a demandé : « Pourquoi ORD-2026-PR-0221 a-t-il été signalé ? »
AI Trade Agent — basis of flag: ORD-2026-PR-0221 has been flagged because the Electronic Bill of Lading (eBL) endorsement workflow was initiated but not completed. The endorsement is required by Pacific Freight Partners before the eBL can be transferred to the consignee. Without completed endorsement, the MLETR-compliant title transfer cannot be confirmed and the shipment booking gate will remain blocked.

What you need to do: Complete the eBL endorsement in Orders & Documentation → eBL Management. Pacific Freight Partners has confirmed availability today. Estimated resolution: 15–20 minutes.

Basis: eBL status log shows endorsement initiated 07 Mar 10:14 — no completion event recorded. Human review and action required.
▲ Exporter asked: "Show verified buyer signals for HS 1106.20"▲ L'exportateur a demandé : « Signaux d'acheteurs vérifiés pour HS 1106.20 »
AI Trade Agent — buyer signal scan (advisory): 2 registered buyers with verified profiles have HS chapter 11 or HS 1106 in their declared import interest and active Vietnam/CPTPP corridor status.

Buyer B-0043 (Singapore, CPTPP corridor): 80–120 MT/month declared, organic certification preferred. Your Certified Organic Pulse Grain record (TPTN-EXP-00841) matches all declared preference fields — currently visible to this buyer in their Discovery view.

Buyer B-0071 (Ho Chi Minh City): lower volume (20–40 MT), no organic preference. Partial match only.

Buyer signals are based on verified registry profiles. Exporter review required before any engagement. Advisory only — no outreach has been initiated.
▲ Exporter asked: "Show greener route options before I book ORD-2026-VAN-1182"▲ L'exportateur a demandé : « Options d'itinéraire plus écologiques pour ORD-2026-VAN-1182 »
AI Trade Agent — ESG route options (advisory): For ORD-2026-VAN-1182 (Hanoi, 40 MT): three options available. Lowest-carbon (Ocean direct, 29t CO₂-eq) adds 6 transit days vs. the current preferred option (Ocean/Rail, 38t CO₂-eq) at approximately +4% cost. Air freight (3 days) carries an estimated 210t CO₂-eq — 450% higher than ocean baseline.

Audit Trail & Record AccessPiste d'audit & accès aux dossiers
All exporter actions — document uploads, field confirmations, AI overrides, order state changes, and shipment bookings — are written to the platform's immutable event log with actor identity and timestamp. The exporter has a read view of their own compliance log per shipment.

Government observers with authorised access can view the audit trail for records within their oversight mandate — read-only, and access is itself logged. API documentation for ERP/CRM integration will be available to exporters wishing to push product listings or orders into TPTN programmatically.

Trust Signals — What Buyers Can VerifySignaux de confiance — Ce que les acheteurs peuvent vérifier
For each visible transaction, the operating environment provides independently verified signals:

Document readiness All documents in the record's required set have been validated against the applicable standard (UN/CEFACT, WCO, IPPC). Exporter self-declaration is not sufficient — documents must pass structural and schema validation.

Standards alignment HS code classification has been AI-suggested and exporter-confirmed. CPTPP eligibility has been assessed against rules of origin. Third-party certifications are attached and verified at record creation.

Exporter identity Each exporter is registered with a verified Canadian Business Number (BN) and assigned a platform ID. No anonymous records.

What this is not This registry does not operate as a government procurement portal, a regulated exchange, or a certification body. Records visible here have passed infrastructure-level validation gates — they do not represent regulatory approval or government endorsement of any exporter or product. Transaction terms are negotiated bilaterally outside the operating environment.

Trust signals are illustrative of operating environment verification logic. No live regulatory confirmation is represented.
ESG & Sustainability VisibilityVisibilité ESG & durabilité
Where exporters have attached ESG certifications (Organic, FSC, Fairtrade, carbon declarations) to their records, these are shown in the Buyer view as part of the record's Sustainability Profile.

Buyers can optionally filter records by certification type. ESG data is exporter-provided and certification-backed — not platform-generated.

Phase 2: Automated carbon footprint estimates for each trade record (per-unit CO₂-eq, standardised methodology) will be displayed alongside the trade record, sourced from the shared ESG layer.

ESG visibility is illustrative. No live carbon registry integration is represented in this prototype.

AI Trade Agent — Import Readiness Guidance
For the active shipment SHP-2026-VAN-04471 (Structural Lumber HS 4407.11, destined for Vietnam), the AI has identified the following import-side requirements for awareness: (1) Vietnam Customs declaration will be required on arrival at Cai Lan Port — the TPTN-validated export documents are designed to support this submission. (3) CPTPP Form AI or equivalent is required to claim preferential tariff rates. The Certificate of Origin is in the validated document set.
Import-side requirements are buyer obligations. This guidance is informational only and does not replace advice from a licensed customs broker or trade consultant in the destination market.

Multilingual Document InterpretationInterprétation multilingue des documents
The AI Trade Agent can explain the content and significance of any document in the validated set in the buyer's preferred language. For example:

"The Certificate of Origin confirms that your shipment meets CPTPP rules of origin requirements — this allows you to apply for the preferential (reduced or zero) tariff rate when the goods arrive in Vietnam."

Explanations are adapted to the buyer's role, not written for trade lawyers. The AI does not translate the original document — it interprets and explains it in plain language.

Vietnamese language support is planned for Phase 2. Current prototype is English / French only.
Destination-Side Single Window PosturePosture Guichet Unique côté destination
TPTN is designed for interoperability with Single Window systems at both origin and destination. Validated export documents structured to WCO Data Model and UN/CEFACT standards can, in principle, be submitted or referenced in destination-country Single Window systems without re-keying.

Phase 2 of the TPTN platform will explore bilateral data exchange protocols with partner-country trade facilitation systems under CPTPP and broader ASEAN frameworks.

Destination-side Single Window integration is not implemented in this prototype. The interoperability posture described is architectural intent, not operational.

Trusted Record InfrastructureInfrastructure de dossiers de confiance
Source integrity: Records accessed by logistics providers are the same validated records produced by the exporter workflow — there is no separate logistics copy.

Audit trail: Every access event and milestone submission is written to a time-stamped audit log. This log is accessible to government observers in read-only form.

No write access to core records: Logistics providers can submit milestone events and exception flags. They cannot modify exporter-originated documents.

Record infrastructure is illustrative of platform design intent.

AI
AI Trade Agent — Exception Resolution Guidance
SHP-2026-VAN-04388 — Phytosanitary Assurance: The AI has reviewed the certificate on file and found no structural anomaly — the certificate appears complete. The outstanding item is a logistics-side confirmation that the physical goods match the certificate description. This is a required HITL step. If the goods match, confirm and the gate will advance. If a discrepancy is found, escalate to the exporter. The AI cannot perform the physical verification.
Advisory only. HITL governance requires explicit human confirmation. The AI does not submit HITL confirmations or clear assurance gates autonomously.

SHP-2026-VAN-04388 — Phytosanitary Certificate Assurance
Government issuer confirmation for the phytosanitary certificate is pending HITL acknowledgement. The certificate is present and has passed structural validation. Outstanding step: human-in-the-loop confirmation that the physical cargo matches the certificate on file. Required by the HITL governance protocol.
Coordination: Logistics coordinator → TPTN HITL Queue → Government Agencies (read-only) → Customs Brokers (if clearance affected)
Exceptions remain active until cleared by the appropriate HITL confirmation. Government observers and customs brokers may have visibility into active exceptions through their respective module views.

Standards & Interoperability PosturePosture de normes & d'interopérabilité
WCO Data Model: Declaration data prepared through the TPTN platform is structured to WCO trade data model fields — supporting Single Window-compatible submission formats at target regulatory interfaces.

UN/CEFACT: Document schemas used in exporter-originated records (eCI, eBL, CO) align to UN/CEFACT D16B and D22B message standards, reducing broker re-entry burden.

CPTPP Rules of Origin: The platform's Certificate of Origin workflow is designed to support CPTPP preferential tariff claims — the broker's role includes confirming the rules of origin assessment before submission.

Interoperability posture is illustrative of design intent. No live government submission interface is represented.

AI Trade Agent — Declaration SupportAgent IA Commerce — Soutien à la déclaration
The AI Trade Agent supports declaration preparation in the following illustrative ways:

HS classification review: The AI can cross-reference an HS code against the product description in the exporter's records and flag potential mismatches for broker review. The broker makes the final determination.

Rules of origin check: The AI can assess whether the Certificate of Origin data is consistent with the declared HS chapter and CPTPP agreement requirements, and flag for broker review if inconsistency is detected.

Declaration completeness: The AI scans the declaration data set for missing or inconsistent fields before the broker proceeds to submission.

AI support is advisory. The broker is the responsible party for all declaration decisions. The AI does not autonomously prepare, verify, or submit declarations.

AI Trade Agent — Exception Guidance
SHP-2026-VAN-04388 — Phytosanitary Exception: This exception originates in the logistics HITL governance queue and is not a broker-initiated flag. The AI has reviewed the certificate on file — no structural anomaly detected. The outstanding step is a logistics-side physical goods verification. The broker's role is to monitor and assess whether the exception outcome affects the declaration or any associated regulatory notification. The AI recommends the broker hold the declaration pending HITL resolution before committing to any supplementary regulatory filing.
Advisory only. Declaration decisions and any regulatory notifications are the exclusive responsibility of the licensed customs broker. The AI does not prepare or submit any regulatory notification.
Open Exceptions — Broker AwarenessExceptions ouvertes — Visibilité du courtier1 active · Illustrative data
SHP-2026-VAN-04388 — Phytosanitary Certificate HITL Exception
This exception was flagged by the TPTN HITL governance gate when the logistics provider submitted the phytosanitary certificate for assurance review. The certificate is structurally present and valid in format — the outstanding item is a human-in-the-loop confirmation by the logistics coordinator that physical cargo matches. The broker is not the source of this exception and is not required to act until the logistics HITL step is resolved or a discrepancy is confirmed. If a discrepancy is confirmed, a supplementary note to the relevant phytosanitary authority may be required.
Status: Logistics HITL gate → Broker monitoring → If resolved: no action. If discrepancy confirmed: broker assesses supplementary notification requirement → Government Agencies notified via platform if required
Exceptions in the broker view include both broker-initiated flags and platform HITL exceptions affecting the broker's assigned filings. All exception awareness events are logged.

Government Review, Coordination & Oversight WorkspaceEspace de travail d'examen, de coordination et de surveillance gouvernementale
TPTN's operating model is designed to reduce export friction — supporting Canadian exporters from market opportunity and readiness through documentation, compliance, review, and execution. Authorised public-sector participants work from a structured, audit-logged shared trade record to support coordinated review, trade enablement, and inter-agency visibility — without recreating disconnected case files. Illustrative composite government user across Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), Agriculture & Agri-Food Canada (AAFC), and Transport Canada (TC) functions. All records, metrics, and review states are representative of platform logic — not live government data, regulatory decisions, or operational assessments.Le modèle d'exploitation TPTN est conçu pour réduire les frictions à l'exportation — soutenant les exportateurs canadiens de l'opportunité de marché et de la préparation à la documentation, la conformité, l'examen et l'exécution. Les participants autorisés travaillent à partir d'un dossier partagé structuré. Hors production.
▦
Illustrative environment notice: This workspace illustrates how TPTN could present trusted trade records and compliance indicators to authorised government users. It does not represent a live government system, active regulatory review, or any production deployment. TPTN does not replace or replicate any government Single Window, CBSA system, or regulatory authority.
▶
When government review becomes active: Government participants in this environment engage when a validated record enters review scope, a field is flagged for follow-up, a HITL checkpoint or compliance exception requires attention, or cross-agency coordination is needed. Government does not interact with exporters or brokers through commercial communication threads, and does not modify the shared commercial record. All review actions are audit-logged with reviewer identity and timestamp.

No direct integration with trade-finance, trade-support program, or export-promotion systems is represented in this prototype.

Standards Alignment & Interoperability PostureAlignement sur les normes & posture d'interopérabilité
WCO Data Model: All shipment records reviewed through this workspace are structured to WCO trade data model fields — compatible with CBSA pre-arrival data requirements and Single Window data exchange standards.

MLETR-Aligned Records: Electronic Bills of Lading (eBL) visible in this workspace are MLETR-compliant. Title transfer records are auditable and traceable through the platform audit trail.

Single Window-Compatible: Platform record structure is designed for future interoperability with government Single Window systems. TPTN does not replace or connect to live government systems in this prototype.

Canadian Data Residency: All records are hosted within Canadian sovereign infrastructure (ThinkOn / OVHcloud Canada / SSC GovCloud — Gate A decision framework).

Interoperability posture is illustrative of platform design intent. No live government integration is represented.

Reducing Duplicate Handling — Design Intent
This coordination model is designed to help minimise rekeying and duplicate handling of the same trade information across authorised participants. Structured record references, review notes, and coordination status travel with the same shared record rather than requiring information to be re-entered into separate agency review systems at each stage.

What this supports in design:
Authorised agencies reference and annotate the canonical record; they do not create a parallel government copy of the case. When a compliance condition changes — for example, a HITL gate is resolved, an eBL is endorsed, or a declaration is confirmed — all authorised participants see the updated status without re-submission. Review notes and coordination status are logged on the same record rather than communicated through separate channels.

This represents design intent for the coordination layer. No live inter-agency integration with CFIA, CBSA, Transport Canada, or port authority systems is represented in this prototype. Integration pathways and data-sharing protocols would be defined with each authorised participant during a structured pilot.
Coordination Boundary — Government vs. Commercial
Internal government coordination is distinct from commercial communication activity elsewhere in the operating environment.

Government coordination layer: Structured, role-scoped, and audit-aware. Authorised public-sector participants record review notes, flag conditions, and update coordination status against the shared record. Commercial participants — exporters, buyers, logistics providers, brokers — cannot view or participate in internal government coordination notes.

Commercial communication layer: Operates separately in the exporter, buyer, logistics, and broker workspaces. Commercial negotiations, sourcing inquiries, and transaction terms are not visible to government reviewers beyond the structured record data they are authorised to access.

This boundary reflects the operating environment's RBAC design — role-based access is enforced at the data layer, not only at the interface. Illustrative design intent.

Single Window Interoperability PosturePosture d'interopérabilité Guichet Unique
Design position: TPTN is designed to complement — not replace — government Single Window infrastructure. The platform captures and structures trade data upstream of government review, reducing the administrative burden at submission and improving the quality of pre-arrival notifications.

Exchange posture: TPTN record schemas are designed to enable structured data export to Single Window-compatible interfaces. In this phase, data exchange is illustrative — no live government API connection is represented.

Phase 2 integration scope: Planned Phase 2 architecture includes tested data exchange with CBSA pre-arrival workflows and, where appropriate, partner jurisdiction trade data interfaces under bilateral trade facilitation frameworks.

Single Window integration is illustrative of design intent. TPTN does not replicate or replace any government system.
Data Quality & Record IntegrityQualité des données & intégrité des dossiers
Capture-once principle: Shipment data is captured at source (exporter) and propagated to all other participants through the Data Exchange Hub. No module re-keys data from another module.

Validation logic: Infrastructure validation checks document completeness, HS classification format, origin country consistency, and standards-schema conformance before records are marked as Admin-Ready.

No orphaned records: Every record has a traceable origin (entity identity, timestamp, platform session). Anonymous or unverified records are not admitted to the platform.

Validation logic is illustrative. Platform validation design is subject to technical architecture review prior to production deployment.
Shared Infrastructure — Auditability & TraceabilityInfrastructure Partagée — Auditabilité & Traçabilité
Audit Architecture & Traceability DesignArchitecture d'audit & conception de la traçabilité
Every significant action in the TPTN operating environment is recorded in an immutable, time-stamped audit trail. This section describes the audit architecture design — not a live audit log. All content is illustrative.Chaque action significative dans l'environnement opérationnel TPTN est enregistrée dans une piste d'audit immuable et horodatée. Intention de conception illustrative.
Audit Trail Design PrinciplesPrincipes de conception de la piste d'audit
Immutability: Audit entries are append-only. No platform user — including administrators — can modify or delete an audit entry once written. Entries are cryptographically linked to prevent silent tampering.

Actor attribution: Every audit entry is attributed to a verified entity identity (person, agency, or system process). Anonymous actions are not permitted at any layer.

Timestamp integrity: All timestamps use UTC with server-side generation — client-side timestamps are not used for audit purposes.

Cross-module continuity: The audit trail is shared across all modules. A government reviewer, for instance, can trace a record from exporter creation through logistics handoff, broker filing, and government review in a single audit view.

Scope visibility: Audit access is role-scoped. Government reviewers see all audit entries for records within their review mandate. Exporters see only entries for their own records. Brokers see entries for their assigned filings.

Audit architecture is illustrative of design intent. Technical implementation is subject to security architecture review.

Shared Infrastructure — Identity & Access ControlInfrastructure Partagée — Identité & Contrôle d'accès
Role-Based Access Control & Identity ArchitectureContrôle d'accès fondé sur les rôles & architecture d'identité
TPTN enforces role-based access at the data layer — not at the UI level. Every participant sees only the records relevant to their function. Access is attributed to verified identities. This section documents the RBAC design for institutional stakeholders.TPTN applique un contrôle d'accès fondé sur les rôles au niveau de la couche de données — pas seulement au niveau de l'interface. Chaque participant ne voit que ce qui est pertinent pour son rôle. Intention de conception illustrative.

Identity ArchitectureArchitecture d'identité
Entity verification: All platform participants — exporters, buyers, logistics providers, brokers, and government users — are verified at registration. No anonymous participation.

MFA requirement: Multi-factor authentication is required for all user accounts. High-sensitivity actions (declaration submission, eBL endorsement, HITL gate resolution) require MFA confirmation.

Session attribution: All platform actions are attributed to a specific session identity. Session tokens are non-transferable and expire after a defined idle period.

Role assignment: Roles are assigned at entity registration and reviewed on a defined cycle. Role changes are audit-logged. No self-assignment of elevated roles.

Identity architecture is illustrative. Technical implementation is subject to security architecture and government accreditation requirements.
Need-to-Know Design PrinciplePrincipe de conception « besoin d'en connaître »
TPTN's access control is designed around the principle of minimum necessary visibility. No participant receives access to data beyond what is required for their operational function within the platform.

This means, for example, that a logistics provider can see cargo dimensions and transport milestones, but cannot see the declared commercial value or the buyer's identity. A government reviewer can see the full declaration for review purposes, but cannot see the buyer's payment terms or the exporter's pricing logic.

The Data Exchange Hub enforces these scoping rules at the record layer — not at the UI presentation layer — so that field-level access control is consistent regardless of how the data is accessed.

Access design is illustrative of intent. Field-level enforcement is subject to technical architecture review.
Shared Infrastructure — Governance & AIInfrastructure Partagée — Gouvernance & IA
HITL Governance & AI Trade Agent ArchitectureGouvernance HITL & architecture de l'Agent IA Commerce
TPTN operates under a human-in-the-loop governance model — advisory AI support with mandatory human review at defined checkpoints. This section documents the HITL and AI governance posture for institutional and government stakeholders.TPTN fonctionne selon un modèle de gouvernance avec l'humain dans la boucle — aide à la décision IA consultative avec confirmation humaine obligatoire avant toute action décisionnelle. Intention de conception illustrative.
AI Trade Agent — Environment-Wide PostureAgent IA Commerce — Posture à l'échelle de l'environnement
Advisory only: The AI Trade Agent provides contextual guidance, anomaly explanation, completeness prompts, and next-step recommendations. It does not make regulatory determinations, submit declarations, approve transactions, or take any irreversible action.

Role-appropriate context: AI prompts are tailored to the module and role context — exporter-facing guidance differs from broker or government-facing guidance. The AI is aware of the access scope of the current user and does not surface data outside that scope.

Explainability: Every AI recommendation is accompanied by a rationale. The AI does not produce black-box outputs — each suggestion includes the basis for the recommendation and an indication of confidence level.

Logged actions: All AI advisory events are logged in the audit trail with context, user response, and outcome. This enables post-hoc review of AI-assisted decisions.

Human override: A human override option is available at every AI advisory interaction. The override itself is logged.

AI posture is illustrative of governance design intent. AI model selection, fine-tuning approach, and evaluation methodology are subject to architecture review.

HITL Governance DesignConception de la gouvernance HITL
What triggers a HITL gate: The platform automatically flags records for human-in-the-loop review when: (1) a document cannot be automatically validated, (2) a discrepancy is detected between a submitted record and a reference dataset, (3) a controlled goods indicator is present, or (4) an anomaly score from the AI layer exceeds a defined threshold.

HITL resolution process: When a HITL gate is activated, the relevant platform participant (logistics coordinator, broker, or government reviewer depending on the gate type) is notified and asked to confirm or clarify. The gate remains active — blocking downstream status advancement — until a human confirms or escalates.

Escalation path: If a HITL reviewer cannot resolve the exception, they escalate to a senior reviewer or, where appropriate, to the relevant regulatory authority outside the platform. The escalation event is logged.

Government visibility: All HITL exception states are visible to government reviewers in the Government Agencies Module in read-only form. Government reviewers do not intervene in the HITL resolution process through the platform.

HITL design is illustrative. Threshold logic and escalation protocols are subject to pilot validation.

Shared Infrastructure — Hosting & ResilienceInfrastructure Partagée — Hébergement & Résilience
Canadian Sovereign Hosting & Resilience PostureHébergement souverain canadien & posture de résilience
TPTN is designed with Canadian data sovereignty and resilience as core infrastructure requirements. This section documents the hosting architecture posture for procurement and government stakeholders. All content is illustrative of design intent — not live production infrastructure.TPTN est conçu avec la souveraineté des données canadiennes et la résilience comme exigences fondamentales de l'infrastructure. Intention de conception illustrative.
Hosting Architecture — IllustrativeArchitecture d'hébergement — Illustrative
Canadian sovereignty posture: TPTN's sovereignty design intent extends beyond data residency. The infrastructure architecture is designed to maintain Canadian operational and governance control across the full stack — not only where data is stored, but who administers it, who holds the encryption keys, and which legal jurisdiction governs the infrastructure at rest and under compulsion. For government-facing workloads, TPTN's design intent is to minimise exposure to foreign jurisdictional reach, including through contractual, administrative, and architectural means. This is a design posture — not a certified legal position — and will be subject to government security review in the context of any formal deployment pathway.

Canadian data residency: All TPTN operating environment data — shipment records, user identities, document sets, and audit trails — is hosted within Canadian borders. No data is transmitted to or stored in foreign jurisdictions in normal operations.

Hosting providers (illustrative):
  • ThinkOn — Canadian sovereign cloud (primary)
  • OVHcloud Canada — Canadian-operated infrastructure (secondary)
  • SSC GovCloud — Government of Canada shared services cloud (Gate A decision pathway for government-facing workloads)
Gate A decision framework: The choice of hosting architecture for government-connected workloads follows the Government of Canada Gate A cloud decision process. TPTN platform components that interface with government agencies will be subject to the appropriate security classification and hosting review.

Hosting architecture is illustrative of design intent. No infrastructure is currently provisioned for production use.

Security & Compliance PosturePosture de sécurité & conformité
Encryption key custody: Encryption keys for government-facing and sensitive workloads are designed to remain under Canadian custody — held by Canadian-operated key management services, not by foreign cloud providers or their affiliates. This is a design intent that will be governed by contract and architecture review in any formal deployment pathway.

Administrative access control: Privileged and administrative access to the TPTN operating environment is designed to be restricted to personnel operating under Canadian jurisdiction. Remote administrative access from foreign jurisdictions is a design exclusion for government-facing workloads — subject to formal access policy documentation at deployment.

Security governance: Security governance authority — including incident response, security policy, and audit oversight — is designed to reside with TPTN and its Canadian operating partners. Third-party security responsibilities will be governed by Canadian-law contracts with explicit jurisdictional provisions.

Encryption: All data at rest and in transit is encrypted using industry-standard algorithms. Key management follows the Canadian sovereign custody posture described above.

Role-based access: Access is governed by RBAC enforced at the data layer, with MFA required for all users. Privileged access follows a documented least-privilege architecture.

Audit and monitoring: Infrastructure-level security events are logged in a separate security audit trail, distinct from the trade record audit trail. Security audit access is restricted to authorised infrastructure administrators under Canadian governance.

Penetration testing: Scheduled as part of the pre-production security review cycle. Results will inform the SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audit pathways.

Sovereignty posture summary: TPTN's design intent is that Canadian sovereignty over government-facing workloads is maintained across five dimensions: (1) data residency within Canadian borders; (2) encryption key custody under Canadian control; (3) administrative access restricted to Canadian-jurisdiction personnel; (4) security governance authority held by Canadian entities; and (5) hosting decision pathways for government workloads following the Government of Canada Gate A framework and applicable Protected B or higher classification requirements. This is a design posture — not a certified or legally verified position — and is subject to formal government security review in any deployment context.

Security and sovereignty posture is illustrative of design intent. No live deployment, production infrastructure, or government security accreditation is implied. Formal accreditation requirements will apply to any government-facing deployment pathway.

Readiness Status Determination Logic  (click any status badge for detail)
Admin-Ready: All required digital trade documents system-validated, no open exception flags, cleared through automated and human assurance gates.
Pending Assurance: Document set structurally complete and system-validated; awaiting human assurance sign-off before handoff release.
Pending: One or more documents awaiting issuer confirmation, digital signature, or data-field completion. Not cleared for handoff.
Incomplete: Required documents absent or structurally invalid. Shipment cannot proceed without remediation and human authorisation.
Exception: Regulatory conflict, data anomaly, or cross-reference failure detected. Blocked at pre-handoff gate; requires human review and authorisation.

Strategic Rationale
Why Pre-Corridor Readiness Infrastructure Matters
CF
Corridor Fluidity
Administrative delays — not physical capacity — are the primary driver of congestion at Canadian trade corridors. Pre-arrival readiness verification reduces dwell time.
RW
Reduced Rework
Structured records eliminate a significant proportion of post-arrival document corrections for both trade parties and government agencies.
RV
Readiness Visibility
Real-time readiness status gives corridor operators and agency stakeholders actionable pre-arrival intelligence.
IC
Interop Coordination
Records structured to open standards support multi-agency coordination without repeated data entry or reformatting.
PH
Pre-Handoff Integrity
Shipments cleared through assurance gates arrive at physical corridors with verified, audit-ready document sets.

Standards Alignment, Audit Trail & Record Traceability
TPTN aligns to international and national standards to ensure records carry legal reliability, support cross-system interoperability, and meet audit-ready governance requirements. Click each standard to expand.
UNCITRAL / UNIDROIT
MLETR
Legal Reliability
Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records. Establishes legal equivalence between electronic and paper trade documents including Bills of Lading and warehouse receipts.
MLETR provides the legal foundation enabling TPTN-structured electronic trade records to carry the same legal weight as paper originals in cross-border transactions. This supports the enforceability of eBLs, electronic invoices, and electronic certificates of origin under participating jurisdictions. TPTN's record architecture is designed to meet MLETR functional equivalence criteria, including reliability, integrity, and control requirements. Adoption context: UK, Singapore, Germany, and others have enacted MLETR-aligned legislation; Canadian implementation pathways are under development.
UN Economic Commission for Europe
UN/CEFACT
Interoperable Exchange
United Nations Centre for Trade Facilitation and Electronic Business. Standardised trade document schemas for structured, cross-border data exchange.
UN/CEFACT schemas define how commercial invoices, certificates of origin, packing lists, and customs declarations should be structured for machine-readable, interoperable exchange. TPTN uses UN/CEFACT–aligned data structures to ensure records can be received, processed, and reused by government agency systems, logistics platforms, and cross-border trade portals without reformatting or re-keying. This is a prerequisite for meaningful Single Window–compatible data submission.
World Customs Organization
WCO Data Model
Audit-Ready Governance
WCO cross-border data harmonisation standard used by customs administrations globally. Supports Single Window–aligned submission and audit trail integrity.
The WCO Data Model defines the data elements and structures used by customs administrations worldwide for cross-border trade declarations and pre-arrival information. TPTN structures pre-arrival records to WCO Data Model specifications, ensuring that shipment data is formatted for compatibility with CBSA workflows (illustrative) and international customs systems. WCO alignment is also a condition of meaningful interoperability with WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement–compliant Single Window systems.
Digital Governance Council of Canada
CAN/DGSI 104
Digital Governance
Canadian standard for digital governance in trade and public sector contexts, developed under the Digital Governance Standards Initiative. Supports TPTN's position as domestically governed Canadian digital trade infrastructure.
CAN/DGSI 104 establishes principles for digital governance applicable to trade and public-sector digital infrastructure in Canada, including record integrity, audit trail requirements, and data stewardship obligations. The standard is published through the Digital Governance Council of Canada's Digital Governance Standards Initiative (DGSI). TPTN's alignment supports its positioning as sovereignty-respecting Canadian digital trade infrastructure — consistent with federal digital government expectations and distinct from foreign-operated platforms.

Prototype Disclaimer: This interface is an illustrative prototype demonstrating TPTN's interoperability concepts, corridor readiness architecture, and standards-aligned digital trade workflows. All shipment records, volume figures, readiness metrics, and KPI values are fabricated for demonstration purposes only and do not represent real trade transactions, actual operational data, or claimed results.
References to named Canadian ports, federal departments (CBSA, CFIA, Transport Canada, Global Affairs Canada), and government systems are included solely as illustrative examples of the types of workflows with which TPTN is designed to be compatible through open standards alignment. They do not imply live integration, active data exchange, formal partnership, government endorsement, or any confirmed deployment arrangement.
TPTN is not Canada's national Single Window system and does not claim to fulfil that function. TPTN is designed as Single Window–compatible infrastructure intended to complement government-operated customs and regulatory systems. All pilot targets and operational benchmarks are planning assumptions subject to pilot validation and are not guarantees of performance or outcome.
